title: Insights screen: spend vs. budget by category, forward spend projection, top-10 items, price alerts, waste report
goal: Ship F13/REQ-19's Insights screen. This requires first fixing a real, previously-parked data gap: price_history.unit_price's unit basis (per kg? per piece? per pack? per whatever the user typed?) has never been stored anywhere, and the three write sites (commit_receipt S-13, log_shopping_list_purchase S-24, log_manual_purchase S-29) disagree on what it even means -- receipts price per display-unit-as-printed, the other two paths take a single ambiguous 'Price' number with no stated basis. E-8's S-21 explicitly scoped a per-bucket running-cost total out of F11 because of exactly this gap (see .claude/epic-8/sub-S-21.json's 'Design deviation' and .claude/epic-8/ledger.md). This story closes it via two ADDITIVE columns (price_per_base_unit, price_basis) rather than redefining unit_price, because lib/inventory/data.ts already reads price_history.unit_price for the E-7 Inventory screen's price sparkline and avg-price display (S-19's shipped acceptance criteria) -- redefining that column's meaning would silently break already-shipped UI. Live Supabase confirmed before writing this spec: price_history has ZERO rows in both households (00000000.../real household, 11111111.../demo household) despite 1157 stock_movements existing -- no purchase-write path has ever actually inserted a price_history row with a real price in practice (nullable p_unit_price / conditional `if v_line.unit_price is not null` guards at each site, and prior epics' fixture testing always cleaned price rows up). This means: (a) the backfill described below is expected to be a no-op against live data today and must be reported as such, not fabricated as having touched rows; (b) the seeder must be extended to emit real price_history data or every Insights feature is unverifiable against real data -- both handled explicitly in scope below.
in_scope: **Migration (additive): price_history gets two new nullable columns plus a basis flag.** `qty_base numeric` (the base-unit quantity this specific price observation covers -- copied from whatever the write site already computed/received for its stock_movements insert in the same call, so total spend for one observation is always `price_per_base_unit * qty_base`, no join required), `price_per_base_unit numeric` (price per ONE base unit -- gram/ml/piece, matching catalog_items.base_unit -- the only basis that is directly comparable across items, receipts, and time), `price_basis text not null default 'legacy_unverified' check (price_basis in ('per_base_unit','legacy_unverified'))`. `unit_price` itself is left completely untouched, in both column definition and every existing read site -- it keeps meaning exactly what it always meant (receipt-printed rate for commit_receipt; an ambiguous single number for the other two paths, now superseded by price_per_base_unit going forward but not deleted, since nothing this story does may destructively alter existing rows).

**Backfill (best-effort, safe, expected no-op today):** UPDATE existing price_history rows to populate price_per_base_unit/qty_base/price_basis='per_base_unit' ONLY where a UNIQUELY-matching receipt_lines row can be joined back: price_history.household_id = receipt_lines.household_id AND price_history.catalog_item_id = receipt_lines.matched_item_id AND price_history.observed_at = receipts.purchased_at (via receipt_lines.receipt_id) AND price_history.unit_price = receipt_lines.unit_price AND receipt_lines.line_total is not null AND receipt_lines.qty_base > 0, restricted to household/catalog_item/observed_at/unit_price combinations where EXACTLY ONE receipt_lines row matches (S-27's backdating and multi-file queue mean several receipts can share a purchased_at with the same item at the same price -- an ambiguous match must be left legacy_unverified, not guessed). price_per_base_unit = receipt_lines.line_total / receipt_lines.qty_base, qty_base = receipt_lines.qty_base. Every other existing row (shopping-list/manual-entry sourced, or any row that fails the uniqueness/line_total gate) is left at the column default (price_basis='legacy_unverified', price_per_base_unit/qty_base null) -- explicitly NOT guessed, since for those two write paths there is no way to know today whether the historical number a user typed meant total-paid or per-unit.

**commit_receipt() (migration touching supabase/migrations, S-13's function): at the existing `if v_line.unit_price is not null` insert, additionally compute and insert price_per_base_unit/qty_base/price_basis.** Primary derivation: `v_line.line_total is not null and v_qty_base > 0` -> price_per_base_unit = v_line.line_total / v_qty_base (line_total is already cross-validated against the receipt's stated total within 5% by the extraction escalation ladder -- working spec Sec7 -- making it the most trustworthy total-spend figure available, and this avoids re-deriving any unit-conversion ratio in SQL, matching this function's own existing precedent of never reimplementing lib/receipts/canonicalize.ts's unit-parsing logic). Secondary fallback, ONLY when line_total is null AND v_line.pack_size is null (the multi-pack 'N x Munit' branch of normalizeUnitToBase ignores its qty argument entirely -- confirmed by reading lib/receipts/canonicalize.ts before writing this spec -- so a pack_size-driven qty_base cannot be safely inverted back to a per-unit-display ratio; skip the fallback rather than risk a wrong number flagged as trustworthy): price_per_base_unit = v_line.unit_price * substring(v_line.qty_display from '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?')::numeric / v_qty_base, only when that regex match is non-null and v_qty_base > 0. Either branch succeeding sets price_basis='per_base_unit' and qty_base=v_qty_base; failing both leaves price_basis='legacy_unverified' (default) with price_per_base_unit/qty_base null, and the existing unit_price insert is UNCHANGED either way.

**log_shopping_list_purchase() (S-24's function) and log_manual_purchase() (S-29's function): reinterpret the existing single 'Price' input as TOTAL PAID for the quantity being logged, not a per-unit rate.** Both functions already know the purchase's own qty_base (v_qty_base / p_qty_base respectively) at the exact point they currently insert price_history -- price_per_base_unit = p_unit_price / v_qty_base (shopping-list) or p_unit_price / p_qty_base (manual-entry), price_basis='per_base_unit', qty_base=the same value, whenever the input price is not null and the qty_base is >0. This is a genuine design decision (recorded here, not silently made): these two flows never showed the user a unit or a per-unit-price concept -- only a bare 'Price' field next to a known quantity -- so 'total paid for what I'm logging' is what a human actually types there, matching how a shopper thinks ('I paid ₹120 for this'), not a per-gram rate they'd have to calculate by hand. The existing unit_price column keeps storing the raw input number, unchanged, so this is additive, not a silent redefinition of stored data -- only NEW rows going forward get the normalized figure.

**UI copy fix (required, not cosmetic) in app/add/manual/manual-entry-form.tsx (both the existing-item and new-item price inputs) and app/shopping-list/shopping-list-item-row.tsx: change the placeholder from 'Price' / 'Price (optional)' to 'Total paid (optional)'.** Without this, a human filling the field has no way to know the number is now interpreted as a total rather than a rate -- shipping the backend reinterpretation without the matching UI label would generate price_basis='per_base_unit' rows that are actually per-unit values a confused user typed, which is worse than the legacy rows this story leaves honestly unverified, since those are flagged and these would silently claim trustworthiness they don't have.

**Seeder extension (scripts/seed-history/plan.ts + scripts/seed-history.ts, committed reusable tooling per E-6's own precedent for scripts/seed-history/): generate and write price_history rows alongside the existing stock_movements rows.** Add a deterministic (same mulberry32(PLAN_SEED + item.index*<distinct-offset>) pattern already used for purchase-event jitter) per-item base price-per-base-unit (a plausible INR/gram, INR/ml, or INR/piece value by baseUnit, e.g. piece items ~5-200, g/ml items ~0.05-2/unit) with small lognormal jitter per event (sigma 0.08, tighter than the interval jitter since real grocery prices don't swing much purchase to purchase) and qty_base equal to the same event.qtyBase already generated (null through exactly where qtyBase is already null, from the qty_missing cohort dropout -- a price observation with unknown quantity legitimately can't contribute a known total-spend figure, so it is written as qty_base=null, price_basis='per_base_unit' still true for the RATE itself). For exactly 4 items (2 from clean_periodic weekly/monthly, 2 from high_variance), inject a deliberate +28% price jump on the single most recent event only (working spec's >15% price-alert threshold, given clear margin) -- this is the fixture the price-change-alert feature is verified against, since without an intentionally engineered jump the synthetic data has no reliable trigger for that feature's test. seed-history.ts inserts these as price_history rows in the same chunked-insert pattern already used for stock_movements, in the same `seed()` function (and wipeDemoData() deletes them too, before catalog_items, FK-safe).

**lib/insights/data.ts (server-only): the read layer, one function per F13 feature, ALL aggregation done server-side via Postgres (RPC or .select with count/aggregate) -- never fetch-all-then-reduce-in-JS over price_history or stock_movements, per this repo's own established PostgREST-1000-row-cap bug class (hit and fixed in S-18/E-11's catalog manager).**

- `getSpendByCategory(monthStart, monthEnd)`: total spend (sum of price_per_base_unit*qty_base over 'per_base_unit'-basis price_history rows observed in the given window) grouped by TOP-LEVEL category (categories.parent_id is null; roll up leaf categories via catalog_items.category_id -> categories.parent_id ?? categories.id), LEFT JOINed from the full top-level category list so a category with zero spend this month still appears at ₹0 (UX doc's explicit edge case), plus household.monthly_budget (nullable -- render a clear 'no budget set yet' state, not a fabricated number, when null; no budget-editing UI here, that belongs to Settings/S-33/E-14 which does not exist yet) and a count of legacy-basis rows excluded from the total, surfaced as an honest caveat rather than hidden.

- `getForwardProjection()`: for every item_stats row with a non-null cadence_bucket (excluding 'unpredictable' -- no reliable cadence to project from) and at least one 'per_base_unit'-basis price_history row for that item (most recent one used as the representative price -- not an average, since a single recent price is what 'next month costs' actually means, per the UX doc's framing as a projection not a historical average), monthlyProjected = (dailyRateBase !== null ? dailyRateBase : suggestedQtyBaseEquivalent/intervalEstDays) * 30 * latestPricePerBaseUnit, reusing the exact cycleConsumptionBase/suggestedQtyBase formula S-21's getPlanItems() already established in lib/plan/data.ts (imported, not re-derived) for the no-rate-signal fallback. Sums to one total plus a per-item breakdown (top contributors). Items with a cadence but zero 'per_base_unit' price history are counted separately as 'N items excluded, no verified price yet' -- never silently zeroed or silently priced from a legacy row.

- `getTopSpendItems(limit=10)`: top-10 catalog_items by total spend (price_per_base_unit*qty_base, 'per_base_unit' basis only) over the trailing 90 days, aggregated in SQL (group by + order by + limit, not a JS sort over a fetched table).

- `getPriceAlerts()`: for each item with >=1 'per_base_unit'-basis price_history row in the trailing 90 days excluding the single most recent observation (the trailing average must not include the value it's being compared against), require at least 3 such prior observations (UX doc's explicit edge case: '1-2 data points' is not enough for a meaningful trailing average -- gate at n>=3, not n>=1) before computing trailingAvg = avg(price_per_base_unit) over those prior rows; flag when the latest observation's price_per_base_unit deviates from trailingAvg by >15% (either direction, since a >15% DROP is also a real signal worth surfacing, though the UX doc's 'price hike' framing is the primary case). Each alert carries: item name, merchant (from the latest price_history row -- may be null for shopping-list/manual-entry sourced prices), trailingAvg, latest price, %change -- per the UX doc's explicit 'needs enough context to be actionable, not just a bare percentage.' Items with <3 qualifying prior observations are NOT flagged and NOT silently included at a misleading confidence -- absent from the alert list entirely, matching the UX doc's 'not enough data yet' framing (no separate low-confidence UI state built for this in v1 -- out of scope, noted below).

- `getWasteReport(monthStart, monthEnd)`: stock_movements type='waste' in the window, summed by catalog_item (qty_base is stored negative for waste per the core invariant -- ADR-0001/data-model.md -- so `abs(qty_base)` when summing quantity), valued at each item's latest 'per_base_unit' price when one exists (else quantity-only, explicitly labeled 'value unknown' rather than omitted or valued at 0 -- a wasted item with no price data is still real waste, just unpriced). Top wasted items by quantity, plus a total valued amount (only across items with a known price) and an explicit count of unvalued waste events.

app/insights/page.tsx: server component, current calendar month (household timezone, Asia/Kolkata, via existing lib/date.ts helpers) for spend-by-category and waste report, four sections in the UX doc's own step order (spend vs budget by category -> forward projection, clearly labeled 'a projection from cadence + price data, not a guarantee' per the UX doc's friction point -> top-10 + price alerts together -> waste report, neutral factual copy, no shaming language per the UX doc). Linked from `/` (Today) and `/inventory`, matching this repo's established cross-linking convention (no global nav exists yet, same gap every prior epic has noted).
out_of_scope: Any Settings/budget-editing UI -- household.monthly_budget already exists in the schema (E-0) but is null for every real household today and has no write path anywhere in the app; that belongs to S-33 (E-14, Settings & cost controls), not built here. Insights only READS it.

A low-confidence 'not enough data yet' UI treatment beyond simply omitting items that don't qualify (price alerts' n>=3 gate, forward projection's price-required gate) -- v1 keeps the honesty via omission-plus-caveat-count, not a separate visual confidence state.

Fixing the pre-existing multi-pack qty_base bug in lib/receipts/canonicalize.ts's normalizeUnitToBase (the 'N x Munit' branch ignoring its qty argument, discovered while designing this story's commit_receipt fallback) -- real, but not this epic's bug and not price-basis related; noted as a residual risk, not fixed here.

Any change to item_stats.avg_unit_price_90d -- confirmed by grep before writing this spec that nothing in the codebase writes this column today (declared in the E-0 schema, never populated by recompute.ts or any write path); this story does not start writing it from either unit_price or price_per_base_unit, avoiding a second half-finished price concept. Insights' own spend/projection/top-10/alert queries are independently computed straight from price_history, not from this column.

Any retroactive fix to shopping-list/manual-entry price_history rows written before this migration ships -- correctly and permanently legacy_unverified, per the migration's own uniqueness-gated backfill scope.
acceptance: Forward projection of next month's committed recurring spend derives directly from live cadences and prices.
invariants: unit_price (the existing column) is never written differently than it is today at any of the three write sites, and no existing read of it (lib/inventory/data.ts's sparkline/avg-price, app/review/[id]/review-detail.tsx's receipt_lines.unit_price display -- a DIFFERENT column on a different table, confirmed not to collide) changes behavior.

price_per_base_unit * qty_base equals the real money spent on that observation, for every row where price_basis='per_base_unit', across all three write paths -- the single invariant this story's own verification is built around, per advisor review.
The backfill only ever sets price_basis='per_base_unit' on a uniquely-matched receipt_lines join; any ambiguous or unmatched existing row is left legacy_unverified, never guessed.

No Insights query fetches an unbounded table into JS and reduces client-side -- every aggregate is computed in SQL (RPC or PostgREST .select aggregate), per this repo's own established 1000-row-cap bug class.
getSpendByCategory always returns every top-level category, including ones with zero spend this month -- never a group-by that silently drops zero-spend categories.
